Regiao.heroTagline: Plateau, mountains and rivers in northern Portugal, all around Montalegre.
Regiao.introBody: Montalegre sits high in Trás-os-Montes, close to a thousand metres up and right against the border with Galicia. Around the town lies Barroso: a granite plateau of hay meadows and oak woods, where Barrosã cattle graze outdoors and the villages keep their communal oven, their water mill and the memory of the vezeira, the shared village herd. In 2018 the FAO recognised this way of farming as a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System, the first in Portugal. About a quarter of the municipality lies inside Peneda-Gerês National Park. Winters are cold and it sometimes snows; summer brings hot days and cool nights. Two occasions fill the town: the Fumeiro Fair in January, and every Friday the 13th.
Regiao.highlightPark: of Montalegre municipality lies inside Peneda-Gerês National Park
Regiao.highlightUnesco: Barroso named a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System by the FAO, the first in Portugal
Regiao.highlightFair: Fumeiro Fair: four days of home-cured smoked meats from Barroso producers
Regiao.springNote: Green meadows, full rivers, wildflowers. A good time for walking.
Regiao.summerNote: Hot days, cool nights. In August the emigrants come home for the summer festivals. Peak season: book early.
Regiao.autumnNote: Oaks turning colour, mushrooms in the woods, and the fire lit again in the evenings.
Regiao.winterNote: Properly cold, with snow possible. It's pig-killing and smoking season, with the Fumeiro Fair in January. Keep the fire going.
Regiao.gettingHereNote: Driving is the best option: the last stretch is mountain road, and the region's villages, waterfalls and trails are spread across the plateau.
Regiao.practicalCar: The municipality is large and its villages, trails and viewpoints are far apart. Public transport is scarce. Expect winding mountain roads and take your time.
Regiao.practicalWater: Water shapes Barroso. The Cávado rises on Serra do Larouco, the Alto Rabagão reservoir spreads across the plateau, and at Pitões das Júnias a trail passes a 12th-century monastery on its way to the waterfall viewpoint.
Regiao.practicalAdventure: To get off the well-known routes, go with someone who knows the hills. Natur Barroso runs guided walks, food experiences and outdoor activities.
Regiao.practicalHiking: The municipality has a number of waymarked walking routes linking villages, Iron Age hillforts, water mills and meadows. Serra do Larouco, over 1,500 metres high, looks out across Barroso and into Galicia.
Regiao.practicalWeather: Close to a thousand metres up, the weather changes fast. Even in summer the nights get cool, so bring a jumper. In winter there can be ice and snow: check the roads before you set out.
Regiao.practicalLanguage: In Barroso, much is still done in common: the village oven, the village bull, the vezeira that took everyone's cattle up to the hills. The Ecomuseu de Barroso tells that story, in town and in the villages.
